questions.question: Explain how the San got their food. Who did what?
questions.expected_answer: The San got all their food from the wild by hunting and gathering. Women gathered roots, bulbs, berries, fruits, nuts, eggs and insects with digging sticks and bags. Men hunted animals such as eland, springbok and hares with bows and arrows, spears and snares.

questions.question: Why did the San move from place to place, and how did they decide where to go?
questions.expected_answer: They moved to follow food and water as the seasons changed. Each group had a home area with waterholes, rock shelters and places where certain plants grew, and moved between camps in a planned way, for example to a reliable waterhole in the dry season.

questions.question: Describe three ways the San used materials from the environment to meet their needs.
questions.expected_answer: They stored water in ostrich eggshells; they made karosses from animal skins for warmth and carrying; they made digging sticks weighted with bored stones; they chipped stone into scrapers and points; and they built shelters from branches and grass or used rock shelters.
